arxiv-1610-08391.title: Schmidt’s subspace theorem for moving hypersurfaces in subgeneral position
arxiv-1610-08391.creator: Si Duc Quang
arxiv-1610-08391.description: Abstract . In this paper, we establish a Schmidt’s subspace theorem for moving hypersurfaces in weakly subgeneral position. Our result generalizes the previous results on Schmidt’s theorem for the case of moving hypersurfaces. † † footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 11J68; Secondary 11J25, 11J97. Key words and phrases: Second main theorem; Diophantine approximation; Schmidt’s subspace theorem; moving hypersurface. 1.

arxiv-1810-07275.title: Ca’ Foscari University of Venice
arxiv-1810-07275.description: Abstract We are living in a world which is getting more and more interconnected and, as physiological effect, the interaction between the entities produces more and more information. This high throughput generation calls for techniques able to reduce the volume of the data, but still able to preserve the carried knowledge.

arxiv-2110-12556.title: Multi-linear products with odd factors in pseudo-differential calculus with symbols in modulation spaces
arxiv-2110-12556.creator: Joachim Toft
arxiv-2110-12556.description: Abstract . We give sufficient conditions on the Lebesgue exponents for compositions of odd numbers of pseudo-differential operators with symbols in modulation spaces. As a byproduct, we obtain sufficient conditions for twisted convolutions of odd numbers of factors to be bounded on Wiener amalgam spaces. 0.

arxiv-2404-11836.title: AI-Empowered RIS-Assisted Networks: CV-Enabled RIS Selection and DNN-Enabled Transmission Thanks: Conggang Hu and Yang Lu are with the School of Computer Science and Technology, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing 100044, China (e-mail: 23120352@bjtu.edu.cn,yanglu@bjtu.edu.cn). Thanks: Hongyang Du
arxiv-2404-11836.creator: Conggang Hu, Yang Lu, Hongyang Du, Mi Yang
arxiv-2404-11836.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Conggang Hu, Yang Lu, Hongyang Du, Mi Yang. This paper investigates artificial intelligence (AI) empowered schemes for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted networks from the perspective of fast implementation. We formulate a weighted sum-rate maximization problem for a multi-RIS-assisted network. To avoid huge channel estimation overhead due to activate all RISs, we propose a computer vision (CV) enabled RIS selection scheme based on a single shot multi-box detector.

arxiv-2502-11509.title: DifCluE: Generating Counterfactual Explanations with Diffusion Autoencoders and modal clustering
arxiv-2502-11509.creator: Suparshva Jain, Amit Sangroya, Lovekesh Vig
arxiv-2502-11509.description: Abstract . Generating multiple counterfactual explanations for different modes within a class presents a significant challenge, as these modes are distinct yet converge under the same classification. Diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) have demonstrated a strong ability to capture the underlying modes of data distributions.

arxiv-2507-18385.title: HumanMaterial: Human Material Estimation from a Single Image via Progressive Training
arxiv-2507-18385.creator: Yu Jiang, Jiahao Xia, Jiongming Qin, Yusen Wang, Tuo Cao, Chunxia Xiao
arxiv-2507-18385.description: Abstract Full-body Human inverse rendering based on physically-based rendering aims to acquire high-quality materials, which helps achieve photo-realistic rendering under arbitrary illuminations. This task requires estimating multiple material maps and usually relies on the constraint of rendering result. The absence of constraints on the material maps makes inverse rendering an ill-posed task.

pmc-11317852.title: Exercise as a modality to improve heart transplantation-related functional impairments: An article review
pmc-11317852.creator: Arnengsih Nazir
pmc-11317852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Heart transplantation (HT), the treatment choice of advanced heart failure patients, is proven effective in increasing the survival and functional status of the recipients. However, compared to normal controls, functional status is lower in HT recipients. Exercise given in cardiac rehabilitation has been shown to improve exercise capacity as measured with peak oxygen uptake (VO2 peak) and muscle strength after completion of the program and cessation of exercise results in loss of exercise benefits.

pmc-11517414.title: Housing tenure and acute lower respiratory tract infection admissions in two Scottish birth cohorts
pmc-11517414.creator: C Hart, P Hardelid, B De Stavola, S Hajna, S Cunningham, J Taylor, J Cruz
pmc-11517414.description: IntroductionEarly-life acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) have been associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Despite young children spending much of their time at home, the contribution of home ownership status, on LRTI hospital admissions is unknown.ObjectivesTo estimate the association between housing tenure and the odds of LRTI hospitalization in children <2 years in two birth cohorts.

pmc-11640763.title: Non-Invasive and Quantitative Evaluation for Disuse Muscle Atrophy Caused by Immobilization After Limb Fracture Based on Surface Electromyography Analysis
pmc-11640763.creator: Lvgang Shi, Yuyin Hong, Shun Zhang, Hao Jin, Shengming Wang, Gang Feng
pmc-11640763.description: Background: The clinical evaluation for disuse muscle atrophy usually depends on qualitative rating indicators with subjective judgments of doctors and some invasive measurement methods such as needle electromyography. Surface electromyography, as a non-invasive method, has been widely used in the detection of muscular and neurological diseases in recent years.

pmc-12469671.title: The Antimicrobial Effect and ROS Redox Activity of Nb2O5-Containing Powders Obtained by the Sol–Gel Method
pmc-12469671.creator: Kalina Ivanova, Elitsa Pavlova, Iliana Ivanova, Albena Bachvarova-Nedelcheva
pmc-12469671.description: The aim of the present paper is to study the antimicrobial effects of Nb2O5-containing nanosized powders. A combination of inorganic [telluric acid (H6TeO6)] and organic [Ti(IV) n-butoxide, Nb(V) ethoxide (C10H25NbO5)] precursors was used to prepare gels. To allow for further hydrolysis, the gels were aged in air for a few days.

pmc-12556344.title: The use of age-period-cohort models in the Dutch public health foresight study
pmc-12556344.creator: M Buijs, G De Boer, MHD Plasmans, H Hilderink
pmc-12556344.description: BackgroundThe Dutch Public Health Foresight Study 2024 (PHFS) provides an outlook on future trends in public health and care. However, projecting incidence, prevalence, and mortality is challenging due to uncertainties in contextual factors like societal, economic, and technological developments. It is therefore crucial to utilize all available data from recent cohorts.

pmc-12578814.title: Ethnobotanical secrets of the Baiga tribe in Chhattisgarh Central India
pmc-12578814.creator: Ramesh Kumar Ahirwar, Diptesh Kumar Bhoi
pmc-12578814.description: The ethnobotanical knowledge of indigenous communities represents a vital yet under documented resource for sustainable healthcare and biodiversity conservation. This study explores the traditional medicinal practices of the Baiga tribe and the phytosociological structure of forests surrounding their villages in Bilaspur district, central India.

pmc-12683794.title: Hypoxic migrasomes drive colorectal cancer liver metastasis by mediating CD5L+ macrophage efferocytosis via NRP2/PROX1 axis
pmc-12683794.creator: Yuqi Luo, Yiwen Huang, Yaoxing Huang, Longzhen Chen
pmc-12683794.description: ObjectiveMigrasomes are a newly discovered class of extracellular vesicles, yet their roles in colorectal cancer (CRC) metastasis remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the functional significance of CRC-derived migrasomes, particularly under hypoxic conditions, in promoting liver metastasis and modulating the tumor immune microenvironment.MethodsMigrasomes in CRC tissues and cells were characterized using transmission electron microscopy or immunofluorescence.

pmc-12904677.title: Evolving treatment strategies for EGFRex20ins-mutated NSCLC: a comprehensive review of Amivantamab’s role and future directions
pmc-12904677.creator: Rafael Alvim Pereira, Milena Tumelero, Wallace Klein Schwengber, Gabriel Lenz
pmc-12904677.description: Epidermal growth factor receptor exon 20 insertion mutations (EGFRex20ins) are a unique molecular subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) linked to resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors of the first and second generations. Until recently, these patients had few and frequently ineffective treatment options.

pmc-13210236.title: Global tastes, local choices: Strontium isotope and concentration evidence for changing dietary input in Roman Nijmegen, the Netherlands
pmc-13210236.creator: Maura De Coster, Joep Hendriks, Hannah F. James, Christophe Snoeck, Gareth R. Davies, Lisette M. Kootker
pmc-13210236.description: This study investigates dietary practices and local interaction in Roman and pre-Roman Nijmegen, the Netherlands, through strontium isotope ratios (⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr) and concentration measurements on cremated human remains from rural, urban, and military contexts, which primarily reflect the geological provenance of dietary strontium.

pmc-13301237.title: Comparison of ECG findings between young patients with cryptogenic ischemic stroke and stroke-free control subjects
pmc-13301237.creator: J Uutela, J Pirinen, A Eranti, A Aro, L Tulkki, V Mantynen, J Putaala, M Lehto
pmc-13301237.description: BackgroundCryptogenic ischemic strokes (CIS) in young adults have increased globally, and in up to half of these cases, no clear cause can be identified. The significance of ECG findings in these patients is unknown. Therefore we investigated ECGs findings of patients with CIS compared to healthy controls.

pmc-13338224.title: Beta-diversity of urban vegetation shapes microbial heterogeneity and maintains healthy environment
pmc-13338224.creator: Chang Zhao, Ari Jumpponen, Heikki Setälä, D Johan Kotze, David A Wardle, Martin Romantschuk, Yong Yin, Nan Hui
pmc-13338224.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The biodiversity hypothesis links urban species richness to human immunity, yet overlooks habitat heterogeneity that can quarantine pathogenic microbiota. We propose the β-diversity hypothesis: increased tree heterogeneity promotes urban microbial heterogeneity and improve human health. Using plant surveys and paired data of soil, phyllosphere and airborne microbiota transferred indoors (AMTI) across 72 Shanghai neighborhoods, we showed that elevated tree heterogeneity corresponds to higher β-diversity in both AMTI and soil communities.

pmc-13339072.title: Nematomorph parasites potentially drive nutritional flow from terrestrial to aquatic ecosystems
pmc-13339072.creator: Ayano Medo, Takuya Sato
pmc-13339072.description: Long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFA), particularly eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 20:5n-3) are synthesized primarily by algae, such as diatoms and cryptophytes, in aquatic ecosystems. Although LC-PUFA flux has commonly been considered unidirectional from aquatic to terrestrial ecosystems, recent evidence suggests a potential reciprocal flow of EPA from terrestrial to aquatic systems via amphibious insects and terrestrial arthropods.

pmc-13346777.title: Genome-wide identification and expression analysis of YTH domain-containing RNA-binding protein family in maize reveals their potential role under abiotic stresses
pmc-13346777.creator: Hameed Gul, Shareef Gul, Gao Jing, Rakia Manzoor, Muhammad Mudasir, Liu Qiuyi, Sumit Singh, Ali Shahzad
pmc-13346777.description: Post-transcriptional control of gene expression is one of the strategies in plants to regulate growth, development, and stress adaptation. YT521-B homology (YTH) domain-containing RNA-binding proteins are essential for this post-transcriptional control through influencing the fate of RNA molecules containing N6-methyladenosine (m6A). Here, we conducted a genome-wide identification and characterization analysis of the YTH gene family in maize (Zea mays L.

pmc-13354118.title: Comparison of force decay in orthodontic elastomeric chains exposed to alcohol-free and herbal mouthrinses: An In Vitro study
pmc-13354118.creator: Aulya Maysita Syahputri Arif, Eddy Heriyanto Habar, Zilal Islamy Paramma, Ardiansyah S Pawinru, Eka Erwansyah, Baharuddin M Ranggang
pmc-13354118.description: OBJECTIVE:To evaluate and compare the effects of two alcohol-free mouthrinses, Listerine® Zero, and Pepsodent Daun Sirih®, on the force decay of orthodontic elastomeric chains commonly used in orthodontic treatment.MATERIALS AND METHODS:Sixty elastomeric chain segments were randomly allocated into three groups (n = 20 per group): control (artificial saliva), Listerine® Zero, and Pepsodent Daun Sirih®.

pmc-13558686.title: Modulating pressure in the Orbitrap improves sensitivity and mass resolution in charge detection mass spectrometry
pmc-13558686.creator: Eduard HTM Ebberink, Elena Giaretta, Arjan Barendregt, Jan Fiala, Victor C Yin, Tobias P Wörner, Kyle L Fort, Alexander A Makarov, Albert J R Heck
pmc-13558686.description: Native mass spectrometry has become a key method for studying macromolecular assemblies, providing insights into structures, stoichiometries, and binding interactions. A key aspect for the transmission of electrospray-generated bioparticles into the mass analyzer is the use of gas for collisional cooling and ion desolvation.

uslaw-usc-t42-s7269.title: 42 U.S.C. § 7269 — Transfer of funds
uslaw-usc-t42-s7269.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s7269.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 84 (Department Of Energy); Subchapter VI (Administrative Provisions); Part C (General Administrative Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary, when authorized in an appropriation Act, in any fiscal year, may transfer funds from one appropriation to another within the Department, except that no appropriation shall be either increased or decreased.
